lines: Best afternoon on this road in a while, and I heard every bit of it secondhand. Can't complain.
There you are! Look who finally wandered back.
Next time, I'm coming along. Save me a seat by the barrel.

effects.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Cellar Door, you said? That's a walk, but worth it on a day like this. Go on — I'll hold down the porch.
Try Middle Brook Cafe up in Jefferson. Dot hears everything before the rest of us do.
Would you look at that — every truck that's gone by today has somebody leaning out the window, talking a mile a minute.
Nobody tells me anything anymore. Head up to Middle Brook in Jefferson and see if Dot knows what's got everybody so worked up.
Half of Jefferson wants to know who taught you to carry a case of glasses like that.
Bet that tasting was something. Renata never does anything halfway.
Straight shot down 10 to Hobart from here. Tell Renata I said hello.
Oh, you'll want to sit down for this one.
Renata's throwing an open tasting down at Cellar Door — moved the whole thing out to the patio since it's such a nice day.
Half my counter's already talking about heading down after their shift.
Wish I could've closed up and gone myself. Next time.
Yeah, we heard. Half our regulars already walked down.
Tell Renata we said hi, once the cold brew's caught up with you.
Sit, stay — the Maple Smoke latte's worth the wait.
Good crowd today. Feels like somebody picked up a block of Brooklyn and set it down on Main Street.
Go on, go tell Earl he missed a good one. And take a taste for the road.
Bless you — exactly what we needed.
Too nice a day to pour indoors, so we moved the whole tasting out here, and then remembered the extra glasses were still in the shed.
Welcome, welcome — sit anywhere on the patio.
Actually — would you mind grabbing that case by the shed? We're short a few glasses.
We don't usually do this without notice, but it was too nice a day to stay inside. Ask around — you'll hear where.
A case of wine glasses waiting by the shed. Renata did say she was short.
A chalkboard by the register: ASK ABOUT TODAY'S TASTING DOWN IN HOBART.
Underneath, in a different hand: the vegan chocolate chip cookie is, somehow, still vegan.
A hand-lettered index card taped to the register: heard there's a tasting down in Hobart today — tell Renata we say hi.
A sign taped to the door: TASTING TODAY — ON THE PATIO, WEATHER PERMITTING. (IT IS.)
